item: Row 429: every path that deletes articles moves the keyword counters in the same transaction
key_paths: src/analytics/store.py; src/database/source_manager.py; src/ingest/email.py; src/backup/artifact.py; src/api/ingestion.py; tests/test_article_delete_counters.py
summary: Three paths delete articles. A source delete (ORM cascade) left Keyword.mention_count/article_count counting the deleted mentions until a whole sweep; it now reads the source's article ids and subtracts their unquarantined mentions under one hold of the write gate, committed by the strict epoch bump with the delete (a failed bump rolls both back). The live newsletter removal now moves the counters per chunk in the chunk's own transaction, so a removal that stops keeps every committed chunk exact; the closing whole refresh stays as the repair of older drift. The newsletter filter on a backup's snapshot copy (plaintext and the keyed encrypted path) recounts the touched keywords in the copy, so a backup no longer ships stale counters. The newsletter attach undo, which deletes ladder sources it found empty, now checks and deletes under one hold of the gate, so an article attached in between can no longer be cascade-deleted uncounted (found by the independent read). Shared helper remove_deleted_articles_from_keyword_counters (R101: an already quarantined article is never subtracted twice). This also closes the cascade-delete stamp case disclosed in row 424. One test per path, each failing without the fix. No version bump, no schema change.
